stories.headline: US forces hit Iranian sites as military action expands across Middle East
stories.body:
American forces completed air strikes against Iranian military targets across the region, according to US Central Command [c4]. The military strikes hit Iranian air-defence sites [c4]. They also targeted mine-laying capabilities [c4]. In addition, the strikes hit communications facilities [c4]. Iran's health minister said recent US strikes on Iran killed 18 people [c11]. The minister said 108 people suffered injuries in those strikes [c11].

Iran responded with strikes of its own in the region [c5]. Iran's IRNA news agency reported that the IRGC Aerospace Force launched a ballistic missile attack [c5]. The missile attack targeted Prince Hassan Air Base in Jordan [c5]. IRNA reported that the attack destroyed several drones [c5]. At the same time, misleading posts appeared online [c9]. Old and unrelated videos from Dubai, Russia, and the US circulated on social media [c9]. Users falsely claimed the videos showed new Iranian strikes on American bases [c9].

Action in sea lanes also caused alarm [c10]. Saudi Arabia condemned an attack on the Saudi-owned supertanker Sidr [c10]. The attack happened in the Strait of Hormuz [c10]. It killed two Filipino seafarers [c10]. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said 17 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz by ship on Monday [c12].

US President Donald Trump spoke about the situation on social media [c1]. Trump claimed on Truth Social that the United States has almost total control of the Strait of Hormuz [c1]. He suggested on social media that the waterway could be renamed the Trump Strait [c13]. Trump also said Iran's economy is totally collapsing [c2]. Reports by ABC News said Trump was attempting to force Iran back to negotiations [c3]. Trump rejected those news reports [c3].

The conflict brought criticism to the US military leadership [c6]. US Senator Thom Tillis called on Trump to fire Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth [c6]. Tillis said there was a leadership void in the military [c6]. Former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation [c7]. His resignation came after reported disagreements with Hegseth [c7]. American voters showed strong opposition to the military policy [c8]. A University of Massachusetts poll was released on August 31 [c8]. The poll showed that more than two-thirds of Americans disapprove of how the Trump administration handles the war with Iran [c8].

vocab.meaning: guided during powered flight and then falling freely under gravity
an extremely large ship designed to carry oil in bulk
have a bad opinion of something or disagree with an action

stories.headline: Germany and EU accuse Russia over attempted drone attack on Leipzig airport
stories.body:
German police identified two suspects after finding three explosive-laden drones at Leipzig Airport on August 4, 2026 [c15, c19]. The suspects include a Belarusian carrying a Russian passport [c19]. Police also identified an individual holding both Latvian and Russian passports [c19]. Leipzig/Halle Airport serves as the home for NATO's Strategic Airlift International Solution [c21]. The program delivers equipment along NATO's eastern flank [c21].

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the incident marked a new escalation on European Union soil [c16]. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Germany is not at war, but is a daily target of hybrid warfare [c17]. Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected Germany's accusations about the attack [c20]. Putin alleged that evidence had been planted [c20].

The German government decided to shut down the Russian consulate in Bonn [c18]. Germany also decided to close the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin [c18]. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas announced new actions [c14]. She said the EU is preparing sanctions against an additional 1,600 people and entities linked to Russia's military sector [c14].

vocab.meaning: official penalties applied against a state or group to force compliance
the side or border region of a military defense line
the office or building of an official appointed by a government to protect its citizens abroad

stories.headline: Devastating floods in Nepal spark major rescue operations in hydropower tunnels
stories.body:
Rescuers in Nepal searched for survivors after a glacier collapse caused catastrophic flooding [c22, c25]. At least 1,204 people are confirmed dead in Nepal [c22]. More than 4,200 people remain missing [c22]. Families in Nepal held symbolic funerals while search efforts continued [c25]. In Betrawati, a local resident waited for his wife's body to be retrieved after floods destroyed his village [c28].

Nepal Electricity Authority board member Amshu Kiran Shahi spoke about trapped workers [c23]. He said rescue teams were trying to reach about 900 missing workers inside hydropower project tunnels [c23]. Difficult weather and heavy rains worsened rescue operations for the trapped tunnel workers [c27]. A 23-member team of Indian rat miners offered to join search and rescue operations in Nepal [c26].

The flooding also affected nearby regions [c24]. In Tibet, China raised its flood death toll to 21 people [c24]. China listed 541 people as missing in Tibet [c24].

vocab.meaning: a massive body of slow-moving ice formed by accumulated snow
electricity produced by using the force of moving water
found and recovered something or someone

stories.headline: Maltese court acquits businessman Yorgen Fenech in 2017 murder of journalist
stories.body:
A Maltese jury acquitted tycoon Yorgen Fenech of orchestrating a 2017 car-bomb murder [c29, c33]. The jury cleared Fenech on both charges by an 8-1 majority vote after eight hours of deliberation [c33]. Investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia was killed by a car bomb near her home in Malta on October 16, 2017 [c31]. Fenech's defense team argued that Keith Schembri was the true mastermind behind the murder [c34]. Schembri was the former chief of staff to Prime Minister Joseph Muscat [c34]. Muscat stepped down as prime minister in January 2020 due to political fallout from the assassination [c35].

Other people have already been convicted for the murder [c30, c32]. Brothers George Degiorgio and Alfred Degiorgio pleaded guilty in 2022 to carrying out the murder [c32]. Courts sentenced both brothers to 40 years in prison [c32]. In June 2025, Robert Agius and Jamie Vella were convicted of supplying the bomb [c30]. A court sentenced Agius and Vella to life in prison [c30].

vocab.meaning: officially declared not guilty of a crime in court
long and careful discussion or thought by a jury before making a verdict
the negative results or side effects of a bad event

stories.headline: US oversees major oil investment deals between Venezuela and Chevron
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump announced an agreement on majority ownership of Venezuelan oil reserves [c36]. Trump said the US will take majority ownership of over 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's oil reserves [c36]. The deal follows major political changes in Caracas [c37]. US special forces captured former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro during a raid on Caracas in January 2026 [c37].

Major energy firms signed agreements worth tens of billions of dollars with Venezuela [c38]. The companies include Chevron, Italy's ENI, and GE Vernova [c38]. Chevron announced plans to invest over $7 billion over the next five years in Venezuela's Orinoco Belt [c41]. The investment aims to expand production to about 600,000 barrels per day [c41].

Officials praised the agreements [c39, c40]. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright spoke in Caracas [c39]. Wright said the agreement is Trump's grand plan to replace conflict with commerce [c39]. Interim Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez called it a win-win deal [c40]. Rodríguez said the deal would generate over $209 billion in revenue [c40].

vocab.meaning: supplies of natural resources that are known to exist and can be extracted
serving temporarily until a permanent replacement is appointed
income received by a government, company, or organization

stories.headline: Israel signals plans for Gaza population resettlement amid West Bank violence
stories.body:
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said US President Donald Trump froze a proposal on Gaza [c42]. Katz said Trump froze, rather than cancelled, a proposal to remove Palestinians from Gaza [c42]. US Senator Chris Van Hollen called for an end to US military aid complicity after the statement [c43]. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited a military post in Gaza [c44]. Netanyahu said Israel will remain on the yellow line until Hamas is disarmed [c44]. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir published a video taking direct credit for harsh living conditions imposed on Palestinian detainees [c45].

Casualties continued to rise in Gaza and the West Bank [c46, c49]. The Gaza health ministry said 73,470 people have been killed in Gaza during the war [c46]. More than 1,330 people died since an October 2025 ceasefire [c46]. The ministry added that over 900 people died in Israeli attacks in Gaza during 2026 [c47]. In the West Bank, Israeli soldiers and settlers raided the village of al-Mughayyir [c48]. The raid killed two 19-year-old Palestinians [c48]. OCHA reported that settlers or Israeli forces have killed at least 79 Palestinians in the West Bank since early 2026 [c49]. The dead included 19 children [c49].

vocab.meaning: involvement or partnership in a wrong or unlawful act
people held in custody or prison by official authority
a temporary stoppage of fighting agreed upon by opposing sides

stories.headline: Ayodhya Ram Temple Trust appoints retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as CEO
stories.body:
The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust appointed retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as CEO [c50]. The Trust appointed Mishra as its first Chief Executive Officer [c50]. Trust officials chose Mishra after a long selection process [c52]. The team evaluated 5,585 applications for the top administrative post [c52]. They shortlisted three final candidates before selecting Mishra [c52]. Mishra said he learned about his appointment through television news broadcasts [c57].

Mishra brings decades of military experience to his new administrative role [c58]. He served in the Indian Air Force for nearly 39 years before his retirement [c58]. Mishra retired from the Indian Air Force on April 30, 2026 [c59]. During his military career, he commanded the Western Air Command of the Indian Air Force [c54]. He led the command during Operation Sindoor [c54]. Mishra received the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal for his military service [c54].

The Trust also made several other major leadership changes [c51, c53]. It appointed Govind Dev Giri as its new General Secretary [c51]. Giri succeeds former General Secretary Champat Rai in the role [c51]. The Trust selected Mahesh Bhagchandka as its new treasurer [c53]. In addition, three new trustees joined the organization [c53]. The Trust inducted Madan Mohan Pandey, Mahesh Bhagchandka, and Dr Nirmala Yadav as new trustees [c53].

The new appointments followed serious allegations against previous temple officials [c55, c56]. Former General Secretary Champat Rai resigned from his post on June 26 [c55]. Trustee Anil Mishra also resigned on the same day [c55]. Both men resigned on moral grounds after allegations of donation embezzlement [c55]. The resignations followed an investigation into cash handling at the temple [c56]. Uttar Pradesh's Special Investigation Team released a preliminary report on June 23 [c56]. The report found 70 instances of counting staff hiding cash in their clothing and shoes at the Ram temple [c56].

vocab.meaning: a small list of preferred candidates chosen from a larger group
the theft or misuse of money placed in one's trust or care
coming before the main part or final stage

stories.headline: Government and opposition clash over accuracy of India's GDP growth data
stories.body:
Union Minister Piyush Goyal said India's 7.8 percent GDP growth figure is real [c61]. Goyal said ministers do not manufacture data [c61]. Data released by MoSPI on August 31 showed real GDP grew 7.8 percent in Q1 FY27 [c62]. MoSPI estimated real GDP at Rs 81.36 lakh crore [c62]. Nominal GDP reached Rs 88.27 lakh crore in Q1 FY27 [c63]. That figure was up 10.3 percent from Rs 80 lakh crore in Q1 FY26 [c63]. India's former Chief Economic Adviser said the double deflator methodology provides a better approach for calculating GDP [c60].

Opposition leaders and former officials questioned the figures [c64, c67]. Former Finance Secretary Subhash Garg made a claim about the revision [c64]. He said growth would have been about 2.6 percent if last year's Q1 GDP had not been revised down from roughly Rs 86 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore [c64]. MoSPI said Q1 FY26 GDP was first estimated at Rs 86.05 lakh crore under the 2011-12 base year [c65]. It was revised to Rs 80.32 lakh crore after introducing the 2022-23 base year in February 2026 [c65]. Sanjeev Sanyal said updating the base year was delayed due to the Covid-19 pandemic [c66]. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh called the calculations statistical gymnastics [c67]. SBI Group Chief Economic Adviser Soumya Kanti Ghosh spoke to NDTV about doubts raised regarding the GDP data [c68].

vocab.meaning: an economic figure expressed in current price terms without adjusting for inflation
a system of methods and rules used in a particular activity or science
clever or complicated maneuvers used to manipulate facts or numbers

stories.headline: India strongly condemns demolition of century-old Hindu temple in Pakistan
stories.body:
India's Ministry of External Affairs condemned the destruction of a century-old Hindu temple in Pakistan [c69]. The destroyed temple was located in Siraj village in Narowal district [c69]. It was demolished on August 21 and was estimated to be 100 to 125 years old [c72]. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called the event a reprehensible act of vandalism [c70]. Jaiswal requested Pakistani authorities to conduct a transparent investigation and restore the temple [c70].

Accounts differed on how the temple was destroyed [c71]. Minority rights group Pakistan Masiha Millat Party alleged people demolished the temple to expand an adjacent seminary [c71]. Its chairman Aslam Parvez Sahotra approached authorities to seek legal action against those responsible [c73]. But Pakistan's Evacuee Trust Property Board said the structure collapsed due to heavy rainfall [c71].

vocab.meaning: deserving strong disapproval or condemnation
a college or school that prepares students to be religious leaders
action involving deliberate destruction of or damage to public or private property

stories.headline: Heavy rainfall and severe flooding submerge parts of North India
stories.body:
Authorities in Uttar Pradesh evacuated 16,784 people to safety due to persistent flooding [c74]. The evacuations took place across 23 affected districts [c74]. Three people died in rain-related incidents in Uttar Pradesh [c75]. The victims included an 18-month-old child in Pratapgarh and two men aged 32 and 55 in Amroha [c75]. State officials deployed 1,499 boats and 1,067 medical teams to support flood relief [c76].

In Bihar, authorities opened all 69 gates of the Sone Barrage at Indrapuri on Wednesday [c78]. The action allowed a water discharge of 5.59 lakh cusecs [c78]. Major rivers in Bihar flowed above danger marks at multiple locations [c79]. These included the Kosi, Gandak, Burhi Gandak, Ganga, and Punpun rivers [c79].

Nationwide rainfall remained below expected levels [c77]. Cumulative rainfall during the southwest monsoon season was 13 percent below normal as of September 2 [c77]. India received 618.5 mm of rain compared to the normal figure of 714.3 mm [c77].

vocab.meaning: moved people away from a dangerous place to a safe place
an artificial barrier or dam built across a river to control water levels
increasing or growing by successive additions over a period of time
